1lābellum: long a (Lewis & Short labellum, with a short a). De Vaan, s.v. lavō: lābrum < *lavābrum, whence the long ā of the diminutive. Ruling: Which authority settles a vowel.

lābellum1, lābellī n.

noun, second declension

washbasin, sink

Classically a small basin or tub.

Examples

  • Theodōrus, priusquam exīret, ad lābellum minimum manūs lāvit.

    Before he came out, Theo washed his hands at the tiny basin.Libellus I, Iter in Lūsitāniam

See also basin, mirror, bathroom.

SourcesLewis & Short: labellum

de Vaan, Etymological Dictionary of Latin (2008), s.v. lavō: lābrum < *lavābrum, whence the long ā of the diminutive.
